arithmetic.proof_method: Exact quotient/remainder partition with monotone affine residuals; seven endpoint-checked intervals cover all uint32 values.
algebraic_argument: Every uint32 n has one representation n=7*q+r, 0<=r<=6, 0<=q<=floor((UINT_MAX-r)/7). The seven classes are disjoint and their sizes sum to 2^32.

For m=floor(2^34/7), 7*m=2^34-2. Hence m*(n+1)=2^34*q+[m*(r+1)-2*q]. In each remainder class the bracket decreases with q, and its exact endpoints satisfy 0<=bracket<2^34. Shifting by34 therefore returns exactly q for every uint32 n.

Widening n to uint64 before n+1 preserves the UINT_MAX endpoint. The largest product m*(UINT_MAX+1) is below2^64. Correct q*7<=n, so subtraction returns the exact remainder in0..6 and output uint32 casts are exact.

For M=ceil(2^34/7), 7*M=2^34+5. Thus M*n=2^34*q+[5*q+M*r]. In each remainder class the bracket increases with q and stays below2*2^34. The approximate quotient is q+1 precisely when bracket>=2^34; thresholds recorded for every r give the complete failing set, not a sampled estimate.
For all nonnegative int32 inputs, 5*floor((2^31-1)/7)+6*M<2^34, so the round-up formula is exact on that narrower domain. Its synthetic uint32 adaptation extends beyond that guarantee.
If the round-up quotient is q+1, subtracting7*(q+1) from n yields r-7. Conversion to uint32 gives its modulo2^32 representation, which violates the required exact remainder0..6.
arithmetic.scope: Complete scalar integer proof for the audited expressions and widths; does not by itself prove compiler lowering, scheduling or arbitrary tensor memory behavior.

structural_audit.exactness_argument: At butterfly stage s, a value is a signed sum of 2^s distinct int16 inputs. Its absolute value is at most 2^s*32768, at most 4194304 after seven stages. All additions/subtractions and final permutations are exact int32 operations.
structural_audit.linearity_argument: Source inspection: loaded values only undergo int32 additions, subtractions and gathers. All branch predicates and gather indices depend on lane/stage/N, never input values. Therefore each row implements one fixed integer linear operator. Agreement on all N basis vectors establishes that operator for every legal int16 row; it does not enumerate every input tensor or prove compiler correctness in other environments.
structural_audit.row_independence_argument: One program handles one row with addresses row*N+lane; every lane is in [0,N). No cross-row data or writes occur. All 384 legal shape pairs have disjoint complete source and destination address coverage. Nonzero base storage offsets do not alter relative indexing.
structural_audit.scope: Arithmetic/address arguments about the inspected source plus finite operator verification. GPU basis tests and separate storage checks are still required; this is not a general proof assistant or every GPU execution.

key_audit.ordering_argument: Checking each adjacent pair in the sorted complete finite-value set establishes strict ordering for every unequal pair by transitivity. Equal numeric values must map to equal ranks; the only distinct finite FP16 encodings with equal numeric value are signed zeros. High-32-bit rank dominates the entire low field. The descending low index field selects the earliest equal value, and integer maximum is associative. Zero padding is strictly smaller than every legal key.
key_audit.scope: Exact arithmetic invariants of the audited source expressions; separate GPU checks exercise the compiled implementation, shapes and memory properties. This is not an exhaustive proof of all compiler or device executions.

cpu_audit.oracle: Independent exact Python first-maximum comparisons, crosschecked with NumPy numerical argmax and both public FP64 references. Key-order audit is separate from this oracle.

case_144.label_scope: One exact stable-argmax verdict for the implementation across its complete declared domain.
